acceptance.1 cannot build or deserialize outside ev: fields are private and readable only through getters; the type no longer derives Serialize or Deserialize. The external-crate probe confirms E0451 for the literal and E0277 for deserialization, and the two compile_fail doctests keep both failures in the test rail. admit_event and admit_event_with remain the only constructors.
acceptance.2 existing tests pass apart from getter: adapter, replay, service, hosted and web-service tests pass; their reads use the getters. The one module assertion that serialized a trusted event was replaced by a comment: the field assertion directly above it already proves the trusted event carries no untrusted marker, and the type is intentionally no longer serializable.
acceptance.3 helper not compiled outside tests: no cfg(test) constructor was added because no test needs a VerifiedEvent that did not come from admit_event; the doctests carry the sealing proof instead of a test-only constructor. Nothing test-only exists in the type.
acceptance.4 audit recorded: design.md 'Audit, do not seal, the other Admitted* types' names AdmittedGithubConfig, AdmittedRadicleConfig, AdmittedAspenRuntimeProfile and AdmittedJournal as proofs to seal in separate changes, and AdmittedResult as a plain record because it is embedded in persisted semantic-merge state and is not the output of a check. The same audit is stated in the events module documentation with the traceability markers; none of those types changed.

survey.serialization: no production path serializes a VerifiedEvent: plan_event returns a RunRecord, replay persists delivery ids and body identities as columns, and hosted writes its own delivery table. The only serialization was one module test.
survey.wire_behaviour: unchanged: no signature, replay, body-bound or selection logic was edited; only field visibility, derives and reader call sites changed.

trade_offs: Removing Serialize/Deserialize is a breaking API change; the workspace survey found no consumer outside tests.
EventSelector and NativeRepository remain public and deserializable because they are wire types parsed before authentication and carry no proof.
The struct-literal doctest names every field, so it would compile if a field became public; a renamed field would still fail to compile, which keeps the doctest conservative rather than exact.
